findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no separate aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resource, so report data written into it (including the vendor roster seed object) relies on provider/API defaults rather than an explicitly enforced KMS key.

The bucket declares no acl argument and no aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls block, so it does not adopt BucketOwnerEnforced ownership. ACLs remain active with default object ownership, allowing per-object ACLs to grant access wider than the bucket owner intends.

The ledger_exports bucket stores financial ledger exports but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration and no separate encryption resource, leaving data at rest protected only by uncontrolled default encryption.
The bucket sets acl = "private" but defines no aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls resource, so ACLs remain enabled and per-object ACLs can override the private setting to widen access to ledger data.

The model_artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no separate encryption resource, so proprietary model artefacts (including all object versions) are stored without a defined encryption key.
The bucket sets acl = "private" without an aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls block, so ACLs are still evaluated and can be used to grant access beyond the bucket owner.

The ops_runbooks bucket containing operational runbooks has no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no separate encryption resource, leaving runbook contents stored under default or absent encryption.
The bucket uses acl = "private" and defines no aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls, so the legacy ACL model stays active and object-level ACLs can broaden access to runbook content.

The audit_trail bucket sets acl = "log-delivery-write", which grants WRITE and READ_ACP on the bucket to the S3 log delivery group rather than being write-only. This lets that group read ACLs and write objects into the audit bucket, weakening the integrity of the audit trail.

The audit_trail bucket receives server access logs from model_artifacts but defines no logging block of its own and no aws_s3_bucket_logging resource, so access to and tampering with the audit records themselves is not recorded.
The bucket relies on aws:kms encryption at rest but defines no bucket policy denying aws:SecureTransport, so requests over plain HTTP are still accepted for audit data.

The vendor roster seed object written into reports_archive declares no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument, so the supplier spreadsheet is uploaded without an explicitly enforced encryption key.
